note: FNS 1160.3 is entirely QC variance procedure — it instructs reviewers on what corrective action to take when they discover the SUA was applied incorrectly (entitled but didn't receive it, not entitled but did receive it, etc.). These are audit remediation steps, not caseworker policy. The underlying SUA entitlement policy that workers need is well covered in the OLG: the 'Standard Utility Allowance Expense Introduction' page establishes that Massachusetts mandates SUA use ('a standard utility allowance (SUA) is used even when actual expenses exceed the SUA'), eliminating the FNS scenarios about household choice between actual expenses and SUA. SUA types (HCSUA, Non-Heating, Telephone), eligibility criteria, verification requirements, BEACON data entry procedures, move scenarios, shared living situations, unoccupied homes, and processing of unverified expenses are all documented across multiple OLG pages. The HCSUA page includes specific guidance on updating SUA when a client moves. None of the FNS variance resolution procedures (e.g., 'the reviewer will use the SUA unless the certification record documents the household elected actual expenses') have a caseworker equivalent — they are instructions for QC auditors determining whether an error occurred.
